An interesting alternative, although I have yet to figure out how to alleviate the O(n^(2)) complexity of it:

You compute a similarity score between every pair of users on the site. Then, every user sees their own front page. Namely, they see what would be on the front page where everyone's votes are multiplied by their similarity to you.

You see those things that people like you upvote (and people unlike you downvote!). If you want to get fancy about it, you can have a sliding scale of personalized <-> overall. Or even see the things that are most unlike you.

It has a bunch of advantages. Among other things, it is inherently immune to vote manupulation. The only people that see things that spammers upvote are the people who upvote spammers.

There are various approximations that may be faster (k-means, etc), but that's the basic idea. In other words, deliberate echo chambering.

Some people may see that as a bad thing. I think, that as long as it is up-front, it isn't a bad thing. Especially if it is a deliberate choice.
